questions.text: What should the agenda tell people so they can prepare?

options.text: Who is invited, the room and the video link
The topics, the goal of each and the time it gets
The decisions made last time and who owns each task

questions.explanation: People can prepare when they know the topics, the goal of each and the time it gets. Who is invited and where to join belong in the invitation. Past decisions and task owners belong in the notes from the last meeting.

questions.text: One person does most of the talking. What should you do as the facilitator?

options.text: Thank them, then ask each of the others for their view
Have the note taker read back what has been said so far
Ask the group to vote on the topic now and move to the next one

questions.explanation: Thank the speaker, then ask each of the others, so the group hears more than one view. Reading back the discussion helps when the group has lost track. A vote suits a topic everyone has already discussed.

questions.text: What should you confirm before the meeting ends?

options.text: The topics, goals and timing for the next agenda
Each decision, who will do each task and by what date
The names of everyone who attended or sent regrets

questions.explanation: Confirm each decision, who will do each task and by what date, while everyone is there to correct it. Topics for the next agenda can be set later, and attendance goes in the notes.
